answer: Proof-of-Serial-Work Windows.** Each identity must submit one unique compute puzzle whose answer is a cipher keyed to a rotating public seed, and the solve window is capped at one submission per node per window. The rule: answers arrive during a narrow summit of clock time, so parallel identities cannot outsource solving without a shared hardware queue. An attacker's cost is the serial latency floor per extra identity plus an idle cycle at the window nadir. Forging many identities multiplies solve latency rather than money.
